To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CAF-HI inoculated together with EPI-HI cells, promote HI tumor growth, but they disappear after 13 days of inoculation.
CAF-HI are not able to persist within the tumor and that they promote tumor growth in early stages of tumor growth by enhancing angiogenesis.
inoculated mammary carcinoma associated fibroblast (CAF) fail to persist within the tumors and that the presence of these cells increases the angiogenic potential of the tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of CAF-HI contribution to tumor growth.
the mechanisms of CAF persistence and its role in tumor growth.
the role of inoculated CFA in tumor development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CAF-HI are unable to replace the stroma of HD tumors, and that CAF from HD tumors are required to induce HD tumor growth in this model.
inoculated mammary carcinoma associated fibroblast (CAF) do not contribute to the development of hormone independent mammary tumors.
CAF-HI are not required for the development of the HI phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inoculated CAAF-HI are able to promote tumor growth, but they are unable to induce HD tumor growth in the absence of the host stroma.
inoculated CFA-HI are not able to persist within the tumor but they are able to induce HI tumor growth by increasing angiogenesis.
inoculated CFA-HI are not able to replace host CFA in HD tumors, and therefore, do not persist in the tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inoculated CFA-HI do not contribute to HD tumor growth.
CAF-HI are not able to persist within the tumor.
inoculated CFA-HI are unable to replace the host stroma in the development of hormone-dependent tumors.
